evidence_cards.content: The nature of the risk must be understood and continually kept in mind by control system developers and testers to achieve safe operation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Reinforces that exception conditions (especially those leading to catastrophic outcomes) are central to system design and testing, implying structured exception handling is required — though specific procedural responses are not enumerated on this page.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening sequence, the sequence shall be halted if a device fails to report completion of the current sequence step within the response time window allotted for the step.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception trigger (timeout) and the immediate system response (halt) during an opening sequence.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device, which was previously opened at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'closed', without an operator-initiated command.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception trigger based on unauthorized status change of a device and mandates halting the sequence.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device for the opposite direction of travel changes to 'unknown' or 'open'.

evidence_cards.content: To resume an opening sequence after a halt has occurred, the operator shall be able to issue a command to resume if the offending device status can be corrected within a configurable time period as defined in the database and in non-volatile memory.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the recovery procedure for the exception flow, allowing the operator to resume the sequence under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: If the TMC workstations or network server fails, resulting in loss of field status at the TMC, alternate control shall be at FCU South or FCU North. The operator shall be able to dial in from a back up computer to either FCU North or FCU south and open and close the reversible lanes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow for TMC failure during opening: system shifts control to FCU South/North; operator recovers by dialing in via backup computer to complete lane opening/closing — directly addresses recovery path after primary control failure.

evidence_cards.content: If FCU North or South fails: (FCU Controller failures or FCU-TSU communications failure) Loss of changeable messages signs and DCUs associated with the failed FCU. Alternate control at the non-failed FCU (North or South).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception flow for single FCU failure: system loses associated devices but continues operation via the non-failed FCU — provides hand-off mechanism without halting the entire sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If FCUs North and South both fail: ... Alternate control units: Direct control at DCUs 1-5, and CMS 1-12 control from CMS cabinets. The operator shall be able to connect a lap top computer at the DCUs and operate the devices or perform manual operation from the MCU. The operator shall also be able to connect a lap top on the CMS cabinet and control the signs or perform manual operation of the signs from the cabinet.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception flow for dual FCU failure: system degrades to direct device-level control; operator must physically connect laptops to DCUs/CMS cabinets to manually operate devices — specifies full fallback procedure including physical access and manual override.

evidence_cards.content: If any DCU 1-5 fails: Field devices related to the failed DCU. Alternate control unit: MCU and manual control at the field devices.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception flow for DCU failure: affected field devices are controlled via MCU or manually at the device location — enables partial continuation of sequence despite localized hardware failure.

evidence_cards.content: If any MCU fails: Loss of field devices. Alternate control unit: Manual control at the field devices related to the failed MCU. The devices can be manually controlled/operated from their cabinets (e.g.: Gates)
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception flow for MCU failure: all dependent field devices must be operated manually from their local cabinets — ensures safety-critical functions like gate operation remain possible even if central controller fails.

evidence_cards.content: Device Override is the capability of the system to allow an operator with proper security to continue an operating sequence through to the end even though any intermediate step resulted in a device control failure, by allowing the operator to input a device status thereby overriding the status coming from the field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception handling path (continuation via manual override) when a device control failure occurs during an operating sequence.

evidence_cards.content: Operational Override is the capability of the system to allow an operator with proper security to issue device commands outside of a predetermined operational event, on demand.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a recovery or alternate control mechanism allowing operators to bypass standard sequences (predetermined events).
